question: What is the primary purpose of infectious disease surveillance?

options.B: To collect, analyze, and interpret health data for public health action
options.D: To punish healthcare facilities for outbreaks

explanation: Surveillance is the systematic collection and analysis of data to plan, implement, and evaluate public health practices effectively. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h1)

question: Which surveillance mechanism involves public health workers actively searching out cases in the field?
explanation: Active surveillance requires health workers to deliberately search for cases rather than waiting for facilities to report them. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h1)

question: Which agency plays a central role in providing disease surveillance and notification guidelines in Nigeria?

options.C: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria (NMCN)
options.D: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC)

explanation: The NCDC is the national public health institute responsible for leading disease surveillance and control in Nigeria. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h2)

question: What is the primary public health purpose of mandatory disease notification?

options.B: To ensure rapid containment and prevent epidemics
options.C: To restrict patient access to healthcare

explanation: Immediate notification allows public health teams to contain threats, trace contacts, and prevent widespread outbreaks. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h2)

question: Which disease category typically requires immediate, emergency notification within 24 hours due to high epidemic potential?
explanation: Category 1 diseases have high mortality and potential for rapid spread, requiring immediate emergency notification within 24 hours. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h3)

question: Which of the following is a classic example of a Category 1 notifiable disease in Nigeria?
explanation: Lassa fever is a viral hemorrhagic fever of major public health concern classified under Category 1, requiring urgent reporting. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h3)

question: Why are nurses uniquely positioned to identify notifiable diseases early?

options.A: They spend the most direct and continuous time with patients
options.B: They are responsible for purchasing hospital equipment

explanation: Nurses have continuous patient contact, making them well-placed to notice unusual symptoms, epidemiological links, and warning signs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h4)

question: What is an immediate nursing priority upon suspecting a notifiable infectious disease in a patient?

options.C: Waiting for national authorities to visit the ward
options.D: Withholding all documentation until lab results return

explanation: Isolating the patient and using appropriate precautions prevents further transmission within the healthcare facility. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h4)

question: Who is the primary local government officer responsible for receiving initial disease notifications from health facilities?

options.D: Chief Medical Director of the National Hospital

explanation: The LGA DSNO receives reports from health facilities and coordinates local disease surveillance activities. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h5)

question: What tool is commonly utilized in Nigerian healthcare facilities for standardized disease surveillance and reporting?

options.A: Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response (IDSR) forms
options.B: Nursing care plan narrative sheets only

explanation: IDSR forms provide the standardized framework for reporting priority communicable diseases across Nigerian health systems. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h5)

question: What is the primary objective of contact tracing during an infectious disease outbreak?

options.A: To punish individuals who caught the disease
options.B: To identify, monitor, and manage exposed individuals to prevent further transmission
options.C: To collect financial penalties from families

explanation: Contact tracing identifies exposed persons so they can be monitored and isolated if symptoms appear, halting further spread. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h6)

question: Why is empathetic communication important for nurses performing contact tracing?

options.A: To overcome fear, stigma, and ensure cooperation from contacts
options.B: To fulfill legal requirements for financial auditing
options.C: To replace the need for personal protective equipment
options.D: To speed up laboratory PCR processing times

explanation: Fear and stigma often surround outbreaks; empathy helps build trust and encourages contacts to cooperate with health workers. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h6)

question: Which precautions must be applied to all patients in a healthcare facility regardless of their infectious status?
explanation: Standard precautions are baseline infection control practices applied to all patient care, regardless of suspected or confirmed infection. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h7)

question: What type of respiratory protection is typically required when caring for patients under airborne precautions (e.g., pulmonary tuberculosis)?
explanation: N95 respirators filter out small airborne droplet nuclei, protecting healthcare workers from infectious agents spread via the airborne route. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h7)

question: Which of the following is a major systemic challenge to disease surveillance in resource-limited settings?

options.D: Overabundance of trained rapid response personnel

explanation: Underreporting, lack of diagnostic tools, and delays in transporting specimens severely hamper timely disease surveillance. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h8)

question: What is an effective mitigation strategy against community distrust and fear during an outbreak?

options.B: Community engagement, risk communication, and health education
options.C: Closing all primary healthcare centers permanently
options.D: Relying exclusively on international organizations without local input

explanation: Active community engagement and clear risk communication build trust, reduce fear, and encourage voluntary reporting of symptoms. [learn more](GST114_U2_T20#GST114_U2_T20_h8)
